title: Stream-boundary heuristics for nested structured outputs with tool-calls and retry semantics
creator: Asha Khatri
description: Issue: customers see broken or duplicated structured JSON in streaming responses when model outputs are truncated mid-structure, when tool/function calls are interleaved, or when retries resume without proper boundary metadata. This ticket designs and implements server- and SDK-side heuristics to: 1) detect chunk boundaries and whether a chunk ends inside a JSON/array/object/escaped string; 2) provide resume tokens and optional chunk manifests; 3) attempt safe local repair (escape normalization, suffix trimming) with conservative fallback to full-response re-generation; and 4) ensure tool/function calls encoded in stream chunks are delivered exactly-once or are clearly idempotent to callers. Goal: reduce customer-visible parse errors by >=90% for streaming structured outputs and provide deterministic retry semantics for tool-calls.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits an optional per-stream header 'x-rw-resume-token' at stream start and a per-chunk 'x-rw-chunk-id' in metadata when available.
Client SDK provides StreamReassembler helper with 'resumeFrom(token)' and 'repairPartialJson' options.
End-to-end integration tests simulate truncation at arbitrary byte/token offsets and show successful reassembly or a clear, documented failure mode in >=95% of cases across 10k fuzzed runs.
Tool/function-call side effects either include an idempotency token or are emitted only after commit-confirmation; SDK enforces at-most-once semantics for non-idempotent calls by default.
Latency/regression: median token latency impact <= +8% in api-2026.03 canary compared to baseline when heuristics enabled.
Feature gated behind 'streaming-structured-repair' config; rollout plan validated in canary region with metrics and rollback.
Documentation and SDK examples added: server streaming headers doc, JS/Go/py StreamReassembler snippets, and troubleshooting guide for parse failures.
implementation_notes: Server-side: augment chunk envelopes with optional meta: chunk_id, resume_token, manifest_hints (first/last-utf8-index, truncated_flag). These fields are opaque strings to clients; server will produce them when model backend supports deterministic token indices.

Heuristic detection: run a lightweight lexer over chunk boundary bytes to detect whether the last text ends inside an open object/array/string. Fallback to 'truncated_flag: true' when lexer inconclusive.

Repair strategy: 1) if inside string, try to close string with escaped terminator; 2) if inside object/array, attempt to strip trailing partial attribute/value fragments until syntactically valid; 3) if repair would remove >25% of last chunk, prefer full-resume path.

Resume semantics: resume_token encodes the last committed model token index + server epoch. On resume, server returns a short reconciliation delta; SDK replays appended tokens and verifies no duplicate tool-calls via idempotency tokens.

Tool-calls: require 'call_id' and 'call_idempotency' metadata in tool payload. If missing, server will buffer call until chunk commit. Non-idempotent calls will not be auto-retried by SDK without explicit 'allow_unsafe_retries' flag.
Compatibility: design must be backward-compatible with older clients — server continues to stream raw bytes when metadata not requested. SDK helpers are additive.
test_plan: Unit tests for lexer heuristics covering UTF-8 multibyte cutoffs, escaped sequences (\", \n, unicode escapes), and synthetic edgecases from internal corpus.

Property/fuzz tests: generate 50k random truncation points across 2k golden JSON templates (deeply nested, long strings, embedded tool-call objects) and assert StreamReassembler either returns parseable JSON or returns a documented failure code within time budget.
Integration: simulate network interruptions mid-stream, resumed streams with mismatched resume_token, and verify SDK discards duplicate tool-call callbacks.
Load testing: measure CPU overhead for lexing/repair at 99th percentile throughput for a single serving node; ensure <10% CPU overhead under realistic workloads.
Security tests: confirm no CRLF injection, metadata is validated, and resume tokens are HMAC-signed to prevent replay across customers.
Canary validation plan: enable feature for 5% of production hosts with augmented logging and an automated alert if parse_errors > baseline*0.5 within 24h.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Merge server PR behind 'streaming-structured-repair' feature flag; release SDK helpers in patch releases with opt-in examples.
Phase 2 (Canary): Enable flag for internal org + 5% of user traffic. Monitor 'stream.repair.success' and parse errors for 72h.
Phase 3 (Gradual): If canary stable, increment 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with automated rollback triggers.
Emergency rollback: server will fallback to raw streaming mode by disabling flag; SDK degrades to streaming-bytes and emits a clear warning to callers.
Docs: publish runbook and migration guide for partners using private deploys (notes on resume_token signing and KMS keys).
decisions: Prefer maximizing availability and graceful repair over strict framing. We will not require model-side guaranteed chunk framing for GA because many backends cannot provide it.
Resume tokens will be HMAC-signed with per-customer key material to avoid cross-tenant replay; this introduces KMS integration for private deployments.
SDK will default to safe behavior: conservative repairs, no automatic retries for non-idempotent tool-calls. Advanced users can opt into aggressive repair/auto-retry flags.
We will not add an additional mandatory wire-level chunk manifest until customers with high-availability offline parsing request it; keep manifest optional to preserve backward compatibility.
open_questions: Should resume_token be opaque or expose last_token_index as integer? (trade-off: opacity for security vs easier client debugging).
Do we require a minimum 'commit window' for tool-calls (e.g., server only marks call committed after next chunk boundary)? Need SRE input on latency vs safety trade-off.
For private deployments, how do we manage KMS keys for resume_token HMACs across upgrades and key rotations?
Is 25% truncation threshold for choosing full-resume vs local repair too aggressive for small-chunk clients?
